name: delete-while-iterating
diff:
diff --git a/app/cache.py b/app/cache.py
--- a/app/cache.py
+++ b/app/cache.py
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
 def evict_expired(cache, now):
-    for key, entry in cache.items():
+    for key, entry in list(cache.items()):
         if entry.expires_at <= now:
             del cache[key]

question.topic: deleting from a dict in a loop
question.prompt: The cache holds three entries and one of them has expired. What did evict_expired do before this change, and why does wrapping the items in list() fix it?
question.answerKey: Before, deleting from the dict while looping over its live items view raised RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration, so eviction crashed. list() takes a snapshot of the items first, so the loop walks the copy and deleting from the dict is safe.
rubric: the old loop raised RuntimeError because the dict changed size during iteration
list() loops over a snapshot, so deleting from the dict no longer affects the loop

answers.text: It crashed with RuntimeError (dictionary changed size during iteration) on the del. list() copies the items first so you can delete from the dict while looping over the copy.
RuntimeError when deleting mid-iteration; iterating a list snapshot avoids it
It silently skipped the entry after the deleted one, but it did not crash.
Nothing went wrong; list() only makes the loop faster.
